subject: Media Literacy
title: Oral Tradition: Memory as Media
description: A fast breakdown of Oral Tradition: Memory as Media for builders.

hook.text: Before writing existed, entire civilizations stored their history inside human memory.

buildup.text: Oral traditions passed laws, myths, and genealogies from one generation to the next through storytelling.

discovery.text: Rhythm, rhyme, and repetition weren't artistic choices — they were memory technologies.

twist.text: Homer's Iliad was performed orally for centuries before anyone wrote it down.

climax.text: Oral tradition shaped every culture on Earth before the written word replaced it.

punchline.text: The first hard drive was the human brain.

quiz.question: Why did oral traditions use rhythm and rhyme?
options: As memory aids to preserve accuracy
